parsed.doc_summary: San Diego City Council staff report and draft ordinance (O-2025-107) adding Municipal Code Division 11 (§§ 98.1101-98.1104) banning the sale, licensing and landlord use of algorithmic rent-setting devices using nonpublic competitor data, with tenant remedies up to $1,000 per violation. Document is the unsigned draft with blank passage date; effective 30 days after final passage.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy levels, and no one may sell or license such software to a landlord. Tenants can sue for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
citation_aliases: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.effective_date_note: This document is the proposed draft with blank passage date; the ordinance takes effect on the thirtieth day after final passage. Actual passage date not stated here (other sources indicate June 2025).
rules.penalty: Tenant civil action: injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and attorney's fees.
rules.exemptions: Excludes software that publishes reports from aggregated historical nonpublic data over 90 days old or public information without recommending rents, and software used to set rents/income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords of residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.conflict_note: Document is an unsigned draft; enactment status and passage date are not confirmed by this document.

unverifiable_exemptions: software used for affordable housing program rent/income limits
